notes: Routing/classification fixtures for the TypeScript quality dispatcher. Each case embeds a small snippet inline in the prompt and checks that the skill routes to the correct rule under references/rules/ and recommends the right pattern. Five discriminating cases plus one non-TypeScript control that must NOT trigger. Run with-skill vs baseline; grade each expectation strictly with quoted evidence. A comparative benchmark snapshot is a follow-up skill-enhance iteration.

evals.name: no-any-public-api
evals.prompt: Is this public function signature acceptable? `export function handle(payload: any): any { return payload.data }`
expectations: Flags `any` on a public surface (parameter and return) as a violation
Routes to references/rules/boundaries-no-any.md
Recommends explicit types (or `unknown` + narrowing) instead of `any`
Notes the escape hatches (`as any`, untyped `JSON.parse`) count as `any` too

evals.name: input-validation-boundary
evals.prompt: Review this Express handler: `app.post('/users', (req, res) => { const email = req.body.email; createUser(email) })`
expectations: Flags that untrusted `req.body` is used without boundary validation
Routes to references/rules/boundaries-input-validation.md
Recommends validating the input at the boundary with Zod (parse/safeParse)

evals.name: typed-client-timeout
evals.prompt: Any issue here? `const r = await fetch('https://api.vendor.com/x'); return r.json()`
expectations: Flags the external call has no timeout / abort control
Routes to references/rules/boundaries-typed-clients.md
Recommends a typed client with an explicit timeout (AbortSignal.timeout or similar)

evals.name: structured-domain-errors
evals.prompt: Review the error handling: `if (!user) throw new Error('user not found ' + id)`
expectations: Flags the ad-hoc string Error instead of a structured domain error with a stable code
Routes to references/rules/boundaries-structured-errors.md
Recommends a DomainError subclass with a stable code (points at assets/templates/domain-error.ts)

evals.name: pii-in-logs
evals.prompt: Is this logging line safe? `console.log('login', { email: user.email, token: session.token })`
expectations: Flags PII/secret leakage (email, token) into logs
Routes to references/rules/observability-pii-redaction.md (and structured-logging)
Recommends structured logging with pino + redaction rather than console.log
Notes redaction must cover nested and error-object fields, not only the top level

evals.name: control-plain-javascript
evals.prompt: Review this plain JavaScript file (no TypeScript, no tsconfig): `module.exports = function add(a, b) { return a + b }`
expectations: Recognizes the project is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript
Declines per the 'When NOT to Apply' gate instead of forcing TypeScript-specific rules
Does NOT emit typed-client / Zod / no-any findings for this snippet
